text:
anya: heads-up — seeing intermittent 200–400ms tail spikes on seq=64 requests when KV-cache hits. Mostly on h100-pool-3. Repro locally with perf binary.

lee: observed same in yesterday's canary. Spike aligns with kernel swap in telemetry: triton->cutlass fallback mid-token. :thinking: 

sam: any link to the exact trace? which path chooses cutlass? kernel-decider right?

anya: attaching snippet from trace:
```json
{ "request_id": "r-12345", "seq": 64, "kv_hit": true, "selected": "triton_fwd_fp16", "fallback": "cutlass_fwd_fp16", "token_latency_ms": [2.1,2.0, ..., 42.3] }
```

perf-ci: perf run: https://ci.redwood/p/runs/9087 — saw 0.8% of requests hit the fallback, but they account for 12% of tail latency.

maria: that sounds like a bad interaction with KV-affinity probe sampling. Are probes causing the runtime to switch mid-epoch?

lee: probable. Our probe-sampler logs show a probe when kv_cache_size spikes > 90% which changes the kernel score epsilon. We might be too aggressive.

anya: Repro script (short):
```bash
# repro
./bin/infer --model redwood-7b --seq 64 --kv_prefill 768 --concurrency 8 --batching disabled
# run for ~30s
```

sam: Quick mitigation: add hysteresis to kernel-decider for seq<=64 and require 2 consecutive probe wins before triggering fallback. Cheap to try.

lee: Also we should check if cutlass kernel actually benefits for that seq+kv pattern. Telemetry shows marginal throughput gain but much worse latency when triggered mid-request.

anya: Will run ablation: disable fallback and run perf. If tail drops, we can push a temporary guard.

infra-bot: created ticket RNFW-4521: 'kernel-decider: add hysteresis and probe-window for seq<=128'. Assigned to @lee, due EOD tomorrow.

maria: also add log flag to emit kernel-weights per-request (sampling 1%) — need to correlate with kv-hotness.

sam: 👍 once we have reproducer, can test a small fix: require stable_best_count >=2 && delta_score > 0.05 before switch.

anya: I'll post results in this thread. thanks all.
